notes:
FOUR colours, and the detector finds THREE. The pink is missed, and that is the failure the Intent cares about most: 'prefer a false positive over a false negative', because a marked word that is hidden is one the reader asked for and did not get.

Only 28% of the pink's pixels clear the cut, well under D-H1's 50% coverage, so the word does not count. Pale pink on cream paper is simply not very saturated: S 0.337 against a paper of 0.141.

AND THAT CLOSES THE delta_s WINDOW ROW 20 OPENED. The two cases are at the SAME delta:

    pink highlighter on cream paper : 0.337 - 0.141 = 0.196
    pale callout box on white card  : 0.196 - 0.000 = 0.196

To find the pink, delta_s must be at or below 0.196. To reject row 20's callout box, it must be above 0.196. There is no value that does both. Saturation cannot separate a pale highlighter from a pale printed panel, because by this measure they are identical.

What DOES differ is geometry. A highlight is about one word wide and one line tall. A callout box is a rectangle spanning many lines and many words. A rule that rejected saturated regions much taller than a line would drop the callout box and keep the pink, and it needs no colour judgement at all. That is a proposal, not a decision: it is new spec, it belongs to F2, and nothing has been built.

Also note the orange at hue 38 and the green at 83 land in buckets 1 and 2, so F5 would show four chips for four colours here -- the yellow/orange collision warned about earlier does not bite, because there is no yellow on this page.
